props.name: ListHeaderComponentStyle
props.description: Styling for internal View for ListHeaderComponent

props.name: data
props.description:
The default accessor functions assume this is an Array<{key: string}> but you can override
getItem, getItemCount, and keyExtractor to handle any type of index-based data.

props.name: debug
props.description:
`debug` will turn on extra logging and visual overlays to aid with debugging both usage and
implementation, but with a significant perf hit.

props.name: disableVirtualization
props.description:
DEPRECATED: Virtualization provides significant performance and memory optimizations, but fully
unmounts react instances that are outside of the render window. You should only need to disable
this for debugging purposes.

props.name: getItem
props.description: A generic accessor for extracting an item from any sort of data blob.

props.name: getItemCount
props.description: Determines how many items are in the data blob.

props.name: horizontal
props.description:
When true the scroll view's children are arranged horizontally in a row
instead of vertically in a column. The default value is false.

props.name: initialScrollIndex
props.description:
Instead of starting at the top with the first item, start at `initialScrollIndex`. This
disables the "scroll to top" optimization that keeps the first `initialNumToRender` items
always rendered and immediately renders the items starting at this initial index. Requires
`getItemLayout` to be implemented.

props.name: maxToRenderPerBatch
props.description:
The maximum number of items to render in each incremental render batch. The more rendered at
once, the better the fill rate, but responsiveness may suffer because rendering content may
interfere with responding to button taps or other interactions.

props.name: onStartReached
props.description:
Called once when the scroll position gets within within `onStartReachedThreshold`
from the logical start of the list.

props.name: onStartReachedThreshold
props.description:
How far from the start (in units of visible length of the list) the leading edge of the
list must be from the start of the content to trigger the `onStartReached` callback.
Thus, a value of 0.5 will trigger `onStartReached` when the start of the content is
within half the visible length of the list.

props.name: onViewableItemsChanged
props.description:
Called when the viewability of rows changes, as defined by the
`viewabilityConfig` prop.

props.name: progressViewOffset
props.description: Set this when offset is needed for the loading indicator to show correctly.

props.name: updateCellsBatchingPeriod
props.description:
Amount of time between low-pri item render batches, e.g. for rendering items quite a ways off
screen. Similar fill rate/responsiveness tradeoff as `maxToRenderPerBatch`.

props.name: windowSize
props.description:
Determines the maximum number of items rendered outside of the visible area, in units of
visible lengths. So if your list fills the screen, then `windowSize={21}` (the default) will
render the visible screen area plus up to 10 screens above and 10 below the viewport. Reducing
this number will reduce memory consumption and may improve performance, but will increase the
chance that fast scrolling may reveal momentary blank areas of unrendered content.

props.name: CellRendererComponent
props.description:
CellRendererComponent allows customizing how cells rendered by
`renderItem`/`ListItemComponent` are wrapped when placed into the
underlying ScrollView. This component must accept event handlers which
notify VirtualizedList of changes within the cell.

props.name: contentContainerStyle
innerViewRef
props.description:
A ref to the inner View element of the ScrollView. This should be used
instead of calling `getInnerViewRef`.

props.name: scrollViewRef
props.description:
A ref to the Native ScrollView component. This ref can be used to call
all of ScrollView's public methods, in addition to native methods like
measure, measureLayout, etc.

props.name: decelerationRate
props.description:
A floating-point number that determines how quickly the scroll view
decelerates after the user lifts their finger. You may also use string
shortcuts `"normal"` and `"fast"` which match the underlying iOS settings
for `UIScrollViewDecelerationRateNormal` and
`UIScrollViewDecelerationRateFast` respectively.

 - `'normal'`: 0.998 on iOS, 0.985 on Android (the default)
 - `'fast'`: 0.99 on iOS, 0.9 on Android

props.name: invertStickyHeaders
props.description:
If sticky headers should stick at the bottom instead of the top of the
ScrollView. This is usually used with inverted ScrollViews.

props.name: keyboardDismissMode
props.description:
Determines whether the keyboard gets dismissed in response to a drag.
  - 'none' (the default) drags do not dismiss the keyboard.
  - 'onDrag' the keyboard is dismissed when a drag begins.
  - 'interactive' the keyboard is dismissed interactively with the drag
    and moves in synchrony with the touch; dragging upwards cancels the
    dismissal.

props.name: keyboardShouldPersistTaps
props.description:
Determines when the keyboard should stay visible after a tap.
- 'never' (the default), tapping outside of the focused text input when the keyboard is up dismisses the keyboard. When this happens, children won't receive the tap.
- 'always', the keyboard will not dismiss automatically, and the scroll view will not catch taps, but children of the scroll view can catch taps.
- 'handled', the keyboard will not dismiss automatically when the tap was handled by a children, (or captured by an ancestor).
- false, deprecated, use 'never' instead
- true, deprecated, use 'always' instead

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Called when scrollable content view of the ScrollView changes.
Handler function is passed the content width and content height as parameters: (contentWidth, contentHeight)
It's implemented using onLayout handler attached to the content container which this ScrollView renders.

props.name: onScroll
props.description: Fires at most once per frame during scrolling.

props.name: onScrollBeginDrag
props.description: Fires if a user initiates a scroll gesture.

props.name: onScrollEndDrag
props.description: Fires when a user has finished scrolling.

props.name: onMomentumScrollEnd
props.description: Fires when scroll view has finished moving

props.name: onMomentumScrollBegin
props.description: Fires when scroll view has begun moving

props.name: pagingEnabled
props.description:
When true the scroll view stops on multiples of the scroll view's size
when scrolling. This can be used for horizontal pagination. The default
value is false.

props.name: scrollEnabled
props.description: When false, the content does not scroll. The default value is true

props.name: showsHorizontalScrollIndicator
props.description: When true, shows a horizontal scroll indicator.

props.name: showsVerticalScrollIndicator
props.description: When true, shows a vertical scroll indicator.

props.name: stickyHeaderHiddenOnScroll
props.description: When true, Sticky header is hidden when scrolling down, and dock at the top when scrolling up.

props.name: refreshControl
props.description:
A RefreshControl component, used to provide pull-to-refresh
functionality for the ScrollView.

props.name: snapToInterval
props.description:
When set, causes the scroll view to stop at multiples of the value of `snapToInterval`.
This can be used for paginating through children that have lengths smaller than the scroll view.
Used in combination with `snapToAlignment` and `decelerationRate="fast"`. Overrides less
configurable `pagingEnabled` prop.

props.name: snapToOffsets
props.description:
When set, causes the scroll view to stop at the defined offsets. This can be used for
paginating through variously sized children that have lengths smaller than the scroll view.
Typically used in combination with `decelerationRate="fast"`. Overrides less configurable
`pagingEnabled` and `snapToInterval` props.

props.name: snapToStart
props.description:
Use in conjunction with `snapToOffsets`. By default, the beginning of the list counts as a
snap offset. Set `snapToStart` to false to disable this behavior and allow the list to scroll
freely between its start and the first `snapToOffsets` offset. The default value is true.

props.name: snapToEnd
props.description:
Use in conjunction with `snapToOffsets`. By default, the end of the list counts as a snap
offset. Set `snapToEnd` to false to disable this behavior and allow the list to scroll freely
between its end and the last `snapToOffsets` offset. The default value is true.

props.name: disableIntervalMomentum
props.description:
When true, the scroll view stops on the next index (in relation to scroll position at release)
regardless of how fast the gesture is. This can be used for horizontal pagination when the page
is less than the width of the ScrollView. The default value is false.

props.name: disableScrollViewPanResponder
props.description:
When true, the default JS pan responder on the ScrollView is disabled, and full control over
touches inside the ScrollView is left to its child components. This is particularly useful
if `snapToInterval` is enabled, since it does not follow typical touch patterns. Do not use
this on regular ScrollView use cases without `snapToInterval` as it may cause unexpected
touches to occur while scrolling. The default value is false.

props.name: StickyHeaderComponent
props.description:
A React Component that will be used to render sticky headers, should be used together with
stickyHeaderIndices. You may need to set this component if your sticky header uses custom
transforms, for example, when you want your list to have an animated and hidable header.
If component have not been provided, the default ScrollViewStickyHeader component will be used.

props.name: alwaysBounceHorizontal
props.description:
When true the scroll view bounces horizontally when it reaches the end
even if the content is smaller than the scroll view itself. The default
value is true when `horizontal={true}` and false otherwise.

props.name: alwaysBounceVertical
props.description:
When true the scroll view bounces vertically when it reaches the end
even if the content is smaller than the scroll view itself. The default
value is false when `horizontal={true}` and true otherwise.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustContentInsets
props.description:
Controls whether iOS should automatically adjust the content inset for scroll views that are placed behind a navigation bar or tab bar/ toolbar.
The default value is true.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustKeyboardInsets
props.description:
Controls whether the ScrollView should automatically adjust its contentInset and
scrollViewInsets when the Keyboard changes its size. The default value is false.

props.name: automaticallyAdjustsScrollIndicatorInsets
props.description:
Controls whether iOS should automatically adjust the scroll indicator
insets. The default value is true. Available on iOS 13 and later.

props.name: bounces
props.description:
When true the scroll view bounces when it reaches the end of the
content if the content is larger than the scroll view along the axis of
the scroll direction. When false it disables all bouncing even if
the `alwaysBounce*` props are true. The default value is true.

props.name: bouncesZoom
props.description:
When true gestures can drive zoom past min/max and the zoom will animate
to the min/max value at gesture end otherwise the zoom will not exceed
the limits.

props.name: canCancelContentTouches
props.description:
When false once tracking starts won't try to drag if the touch moves.
The default value is true.

props.name: centerContent
props.description:
When true the scroll view automatically centers the content when the
content is smaller than the scroll view bounds; when the content is
larger than the scroll view this property has no effect. The default
value is false.

props.name: contentInset
props.description:
The amount by which the scroll view content is inset from the edges of the scroll view.
Defaults to {0, 0, 0, 0}.

props.name: contentOffset
props.description:
Used to manually set the starting scroll offset.
The default value is {x: 0, y: 0}

props.name: contentInsetAdjustmentBehavior
props.description:
This property specifies how the safe area insets are used to modify the content area of the scroll view.
The default value of this property is "never".

props.name: directionalLockEnabled
props.description:
When true the ScrollView will try to lock to only vertical or horizontal
scrolling while dragging.  The default value is false.

props.name: indicatorStyle
props.description:
The style of the scroll indicators.
- default (the default), same as black.
- black, scroll indicator is black. This style is good against
  a white content background.
- white, scroll indicator is white. This style is good against
  a black content background.

props.name: maintainVisibleContentPosition
props.description:
When set, the scroll view will adjust the scroll position so that the first child
that is currently visible and at or beyond minIndexForVisible will not change position.
This is useful for lists that are loading content in both directions, e.g. a chat thread,
where new messages coming in might otherwise cause the scroll position to jump. A value
of 0 is common, but other values such as 1 can be used to skip loading spinners or other
content that should not maintain position.

The optional autoscrollToTopThreshold can be used to make the content automatically scroll
to the top after making the adjustment if the user was within the threshold of the top
before the adjustment was made. This is also useful for chat-like applications where you
want to see new messages scroll into place, but not if the user has scrolled up a ways and
it would be disruptive to scroll a bunch.

Caveat 1: Reordering elements in the scrollview with this enabled will probably cause
jumpiness and jank. It can be fixed, but there are currently no plans to do so. For now,
don't re-order the content of any ScrollViews or Lists that use this feature.

Caveat 2: This uses contentOffset and frame.origin in native code to compute visibility.
Occlusion, transforms, and other complexity won't be taken into account as to whether
content is "visible" or not.

props.name: maximumZoomScale
props.description: The maximum allowed zoom scale. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: minimumZoomScale
props.description: The minimum allowed zoom scale. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: onScrollAnimationEnd
props.description: Called when a scrolling animation ends.

props.name: pinchGestureEnabled
props.description:
When true, ScrollView allows use of pinch gestures to zoom in and out.
The default value is true.

props.name: scrollEventThrottle
props.description:
Limits how often scroll events will be fired while scrolling, specified as
a time interval in ms. This may be useful when expensive work is performed
in response to scrolling. Values <= `16` will disable throttling,
regardless of the refresh rate of the device.

props.name: scrollIndicatorInsets
props.description:
The amount by which the scroll view indicators are inset from the edges of the scroll view.
This should normally be set to the same value as the contentInset.
Defaults to {0, 0, 0, 0}.

props.name: scrollToOverflowEnabled
props.description:
When true, the scroll view can be programmatically scrolled beyond its
content size. The default value is false.

props.name: scrollsToTop
props.description:
When true the scroll view scrolls to top when the status bar is tapped.
The default value is true.

props.name: snapToAlignment
props.description:
When `snapToInterval` is set, `snapToAlignment` will define the relationship of the snapping to the scroll view.
     - `start` (the default) will align the snap at the left (horizontal) or top (vertical)
     - `center` will align the snap in the center
     - `end` will align the snap at the right (horizontal) or bottom (vertical)

props.name: onScrollToTop
props.description: Fires when the scroll view scrolls to top after the status bar has been tapped

props.name: zoomScale
props.description: The current scale of the scroll view content. The default value is 1.0.

props.name: endFillColor
props.description:
Sometimes a scrollview takes up more space than its content fills.
When this is the case, this prop will fill the rest of the
scrollview with a color to avoid setting a background and creating
unnecessary overdraw. This is an advanced optimization that is not
needed in the general case.

props.name: scrollPerfTag
props.description:
Tag used to log scroll performance on this scroll view. Will force
momentum events to be turned on (see sendMomentumEvents). This doesn't do
anything out of the box and you need to implement a custom native
FpsListener for it to be useful.

props.name: overScrollMode
props.description:
Used to override default value of overScroll mode.

  Possible values:
   - 'auto' - Default value, allow a user to over-scroll this view only if the content is large enough to meaningfully scroll.
   - 'always' - Always allow a user to over-scroll this view.
   - 'never' - Never allow a user to over-scroll this view.

props.name: nestedScrollEnabled
props.description: Enables nested scrolling for Android API level 21+. Nested scrolling is supported by default on iOS.

props.name: fadingEdgeLength
props.description:
Controls the fading effect at the edges of the scroll content.

A value greater than 0 will apply the fading effect, indicating more content is available
to scroll.

You can specify a single number to apply the same fading length to both edges.
Alternatively, use an object with `start` and `end` properties to set different
fading lengths for the start and end of the scroll content.

The default value is 0.

props.name: persistentScrollbar
props.description: Causes the scrollbars not to turn transparent when they are not in use. The default value is false.

props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:

where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,

So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: accessibilityHint
props.description: An accessibility hint helps users understand what will happen when they perform an action on the accessibility element when that result is not obvious from the accessibility label.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

props.name: removeClippedSubviews
props.description:
This is a special performance property exposed by RCTView and is useful for scrolling content when there are many subviews,
most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.
The subviews must also have overflow: hidden, as should the containing view (or one of its superviews).

props.name: nativeID
props.description: Used to reference react managed views from native code.

props.name: collapsable
props.description:
Views that are only used to layout their children or otherwise don't draw anything
may be automatically removed from the native hierarchy as an optimization.
Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: collapsableChildren
props.description:
Setting to false prevents direct children of the view from being removed
from the native view hierarchy, similar to the effect of setting
`collapsable={false}` on each child.

props.name: onBlur
props.description:
Callback that is called when the view is blurred.

Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: onFocus
props.description:
Callback that is called when the view is focused.

Note: This will only be called if the view is focusable.

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:

it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input is focused

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: focusable
props.description: Whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: isTVSelectable
props.description:
*(Apple TV only)* When set to true, this view will be focusable
and navigable using the Apple TV remote.

props.name: hasTVPreferredFocus
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be set to true to force the Apple TV focus engine to move focus to this view.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceX
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxShiftDistanceY
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 2.0.

props.name: tvParallaxTiltAngle
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 0.05.

props.name: tvParallaxMagnification
props.description: *(Apple TV only)* May be used to change the appearance of the Apple TV parallax effect when this view goes in or out of focus.  Defaults to 1.0.

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponder
props.description: Does this view want to become responder on the start of a touch?

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponder
props.description: Called for every touch move on the View when it is not the responder: does this view want to "claim" touch responsiveness?

props.name: onResponderEnd
props.description: If the View returns true and attempts to become the responder, one of the following will happen:

props.name: onResponderGrant
props.description:
The View is now responding for touch events.
This is the time to highlight and show the user what is happening

props.name: onResponderReject
props.description: Something else is the responder right now and will not release it

props.name: onResponderMove
props.description: The user is moving their finger

props.name: onResponderRelease
props.description: Fired at the end of the touch, ie "touchUp"

props.name: onResponderTerminationRequest
props.description:
Something else wants to become responder.
Should this view release the responder? Returning true allows release

props.name: onResponderTerminate
props.description:
The responder has been taken from the View.
Might be taken by other views after a call to onResponderTerminationRequest,
or might be taken by the OS without asking (happens with control center/ notification center on iOS)

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.name: onMoveShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34424

props.name: accessibilityRole
props.description: Accessibility Role tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the type of element that is focused on.

props.name: accessibilityState
props.description: Accessibility State tells a person using either VoiceOver on iOS or TalkBack on Android the state of the element currently focused on.

props.name: aria-busy
props.description:
alias for accessibilityState

see https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitystate

props.name: accessibilityValue
props.description:
Represents the current value of a component. It can be a textual description of a component's value, or for range-based components, such as sliders and progress bars,
it contains range information (minimum, current, and maximum).

props.name: onAccessibilityAction
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs an accessibility custom action.

props.name: importantForAccessibility
props.description: [Android] Controlling if a view fires accessibility events and if it is reported to accessibility services.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description:
A value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within

props.name: role
props.description: Indicates to accessibility services to treat UI component like a specific role.

props.name: accessibilityLabelledBy
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description:
A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element
are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description:
By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. The provided string value must follow the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47).
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylanguage-ios

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer.
Available on iOS 13.0+
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description:
When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer.
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description:
Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing
screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: onPressIn
props.description: Callback that is called when a touch is engaged.

props.name: onPressOut

props.name: onContentSizeChange
props.description:
Callback that is called when the text input's content size changes.
This will be called with
`{ nativeEvent: { contentSize: { width, height } } }`.

Only called for multiline text inputs.

props.name: onScroll
props.description:
Invoked on content scroll with

May also contain other properties from ScrollEvent but on Android contentSize is not provided for performance reasons.

props.name: scrollEnabled
props.description: If false, scrolling of the text view will be disabled. The default value is true. Only works with multiline={true}

props.name: allowFontScaling
props.description:

The default is `true`.

props.name: autoCapitalize
props.description:
Can tell TextInput to automatically capitalize certain characters.

props.name: autoComplete

props.name: autoCorrect
props.description:
If false, disables auto-correct.
The default value is true.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description:
If true, focuses the input on componentDidMount.
The default value is false.

props.name: blurOnSubmit
props.description:
If `true`, the text field will blur when submitted.
The default value is true for single-line fields and false for
multiline fields. Note that for multiline fields, setting `blurOnSubmit`
to `true` means that pressing return will blur the field and trigger the
`onSubmitEditing` event instead of inserting a newline into the field.

props.name: submitBehavior
props.description:
When the return key is pressed,

For single line inputs:

- `'newline`' defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`
- `undefined` defaults to `'blurAndSubmit'`

For multiline inputs:

- `'newline'` adds a newline
- `undefined` defaults to `'newline'`

For both single line and multiline inputs:

- `'submit'` will only send a submit event and not blur the input
- `'blurAndSubmit`' will both blur the input and send a submit event

props.name: caretHidden
props.description: If true, caret is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: contextMenuHidden
props.description: If true, context menu is hidden. The default value is false.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description:
Provides an initial value that will change when the user starts typing.
Useful for simple use-cases where you don't want to deal with listening to events
and updating the value prop to keep the controlled state in sync.

props.name: editable
props.description: If false, text is not editable. The default value is true.

props.name: keyboardType
props.description:
enum("default", 'numeric', 'email-address', "ascii-capable", 'numbers-and-punctuation', 'url', 'number-pad', 'phone-pad', 'name-phone-pad',
'decimal-pad', 'twitter', 'web-search', 'visible-password')
Determines which keyboard to open, e.g.numeric.
The following values work across platforms: - default - numeric - email-address - phone-pad
The following values work on iOS: - ascii-capable - numbers-and-punctuation - url - number-pad - name-phone-pad - decimal-pad - twitter - web-search
The following values work on Android: - visible-password

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Works like the inputmode attribute in HTML, it determines which keyboard to open, e.g. numeric and has precedence over keyboardType.

props.name: maxLength
props.description:
Limits the maximum number of characters that can be entered.
Use this instead of implementing the logic in JS to avoid flicker.

props.name: multiline
props.description: If true, the text input can be multiple lines. The default value is false.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Callback that is called when the text input's text changes.

props.name: onEndEditing

props.name: onSelectionChange

props.name: onSubmitEditing

props.name: onKeyPress
props.description:
Callback that is called when a key is pressed.
This will be called with

where keyValue is 'Enter' or 'Backspace' for respective keys and the typed-in character otherwise including ' ' for space.

Note: on Android only the inputs from soft keyboard are handled, not the hardware keyboard inputs.

props.name: placeholder

props.name: placeholderTextColor

props.name: readOnly
props.description: If `true`, text is not editable. The default value is `false`.

props.name: returnKeyType
props.description:
enum('default', 'go', 'google', 'join', 'next', 'route', 'search', 'send', 'yahoo', 'done', 'emergency-call')

props.name: enterKeyHint
props.description:
Determines what text should be shown to the return key on virtual keyboards.
Has precedence over the returnKeyType prop.

props.name: secureTextEntry
props.description:
If true, the text input obscures the text entered so that sensitive text like passwords stay secure.
The default value is false.

props.name: selectTextOnFocus
props.description: If true, all text will automatically be selected on focus

props.name: selection
props.description:
The start and end of the text input's selection. Set start and end to

props.name: selectionColor
props.description: The highlight (and cursor on ios) color of the text input

props.name: textAlign
props.description: Align the input text to the left, center, or right sides of the input field.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewID
props.description:

code.
See https://reactnative.dev/docs/inputaccessoryview for more information.

props.name: inputAccessoryViewButtonLabel

props.name: value
props.description:
The value to show for the text input. TextInput is a controlled component,
which means the native value will be forced to match this value prop if provided.
For most uses this works great, but in some cases this may cause flickering - one common cause is preventing edits by keeping value the same.
In addition to simply setting the same value, either set editable={false},
or set/update maxLength to prevent unwanted edits without flicker.

props.name: maxFontSizeMultiplier
props.description:
Specifies largest possible scale a font can reach when allowFontScaling is enabled. Possible values:

props.name: clearTextOnFocus

props.name: dataDetectorTypes
props.description:
Determines the types of data converted to clickable URLs in the text input.

Possible values for `dataDetectorTypes` are:

- `'link'`
- `'address'`
- `'calendarEvent'`
- `'none'`

props.name: enablesReturnKeyAutomatically
props.description:
If true, the keyboard disables the return key when there is no text and automatically enables it when there is text.
The default value is false.

props.name: keyboardAppearance

props.name: passwordRules

Provide rules for your password.
For example, say you want to require a password with at least eight characters consisting of a mix of uppercase and lowercase letters, at least one number, and at most two consecutive characters.
"required: upper; required: lower; required: digit; max-consecutive: 2; minlength: 8;"

props.description: Set line break strategy on iOS.

props.name: lineBreakModeIOS
props.description: Set line break mode on iOS.

props.name: smartInsertDelete
props.description:
If `false`, the iOS system will not insert an extra space after a paste operation
neither delete one or two spaces after a cut or delete operation.

props.name: importantForAutofill

props.name: numberOfLines

props.description:
The mask format to be applied to the text input.
The mask

props.name: disabledInputStyle

```

props.description:
This defines how far a touch event can start away from the view.
Typical interface guidelines recommend touch targets that are at least
30 - 40 points/density-independent pixels. If a Touchable view has
a height of 20 the touchable height can be extended to 40 with

NOTE The touch area never extends past the parent view bounds and
the Z-index of sibling views always takes precedence if a touch
hits two overlapping views.

props.name: needsOffscreenAlphaCompositing
props.description:
Whether this view needs to rendered offscreen and composited with an alpha in order to preserve 100% correct colors and blending behavior.
The default (false) falls back to drawing the component and its children
with an alpha applied to the paint used to draw each element instead of rendering the full component offscreen and compositing it back with an alpha value.
This default may be noticeable and undesired in the case where the View you are setting an opacity on
has multiple overlapping elements (e.g. multiple overlapping Views, or text and a background).

Rendering offscreen to preserve correct alpha behavior is extremely expensive
and hard to debug for non-native developers, which is why it is not turned on by default.
If you do need to enable this property for an animation,
consider combining it with renderToHardwareTextureAndroid if the view contents are static (i.e. it doesn't need to be redrawn each frame).
If that property is enabled, this View will be rendered off-screen once,
saved in a hardware texture, and then composited onto the screen with an alpha each frame without having to switch rendering targets on the GPU.

most of which are offscreen. For this property to be effective, it must be applied to a view that contains many subviews that extend outside its bound.

props.description:

Set this property to false to disable this optimization and ensure that this View exists in the native view hierarchy.

props.name: onFocus

props.name: renderToHardwareTextureAndroid
props.description:
Whether this view should render itself (and all of its children) into a single hardware texture on the GPU.

On Android, this is useful for animations and interactions that only modify opacity, rotation, translation, and/or scale:
in those cases, the view doesn't have to be redrawn and display lists don't need to be re-executed. The texture can just be
re-used and re-composited with different parameters. The downside is that this can use up limited video memory, so this prop should be set back to false at the end of the interaction/animation.

props.name: tabIndex
props.description:
Indicates whether this `View` should be focusable with a non-touch input device, eg. receive focus with a hardware keyboard.
See https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/tabindex
for more details.

Supports the following values:
-  0 (View is focusable)
- -1 (View is not focusable)

props.name: shouldRasterizeIOS
props.description:
Whether this view should be rendered as a bitmap before compositing.

On iOS, this is useful for animations and interactions that do not modify this component's dimensions nor its children;
for example, when translating the position of a static view, rasterization allows the renderer to reuse a cached bitmap of a static view
and quickly composite it during each frame.

Rasterization incurs an off-screen drawing pass and the bitmap consumes memory.
Test and measure when using this property.

props.name: onResponderTerminate

props.name: onStartShouldSetResponderCapture
props.description:
onStartShouldSetResponder and onMoveShouldSetResponder are called with a bubbling pattern,
where the deepest node is called first.
That means that the deepest component will become responder when multiple Views return true for *ShouldSetResponder handlers.
This is desirable in most cases, because it makes sure all controls and buttons are usable.

However, sometimes a parent will want to make sure that it becomes responder.
This can be handled by using the capture phase.
Before the responder system bubbles up from the deepest component,
it will do a capture phase, firing on*ShouldSetResponderCapture.
So if a parent View wants to prevent the child from becoming responder on a touch start,
it should have a onStartShouldSetResponderCapture handler which returns true.

props.description:
Identifies the element that labels the element it is applied to. When the assistive technology focuses on the component with this props,
the text is read aloud. The value should should match the nativeID of the related element.

props.name: accessibilityLiveRegion
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: aria-live
props.description:
Indicates to accessibility services whether the user should be notified
when this view changes. Works for Android API >= 19 only.

props.name: screenReaderFocusable
props.description: Enables the view to be screen reader focusable, not keyboard focusable.

props.name: accessibilityElementsHidden
props.description:
A Boolean value indicating whether the accessibility elements contained within this accessibility element
are hidden to the screen reader.

props.name: accessibilityViewIsModal
props.description: A Boolean value indicating whether VoiceOver should ignore the elements within views that are siblings of the receiver.

props.name: onAccessibilityEscape
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the escape gesture (scrub with two fingers).

props.name: onAccessibilityTap
props.description: When `accessible` is true, the system will try to invoke this function when the user performs accessibility tap gesture.

props.name: onMagicTap
props.description: When accessible is true, the system will invoke this function when the user performs the magic tap gesture.

props.name: accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors
props.description: https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityignoresinvertcolorsios

props.name: accessibilityLanguage
props.description:
By using the accessibilityLanguage property, the screen reader will understand which language to use while reading the element's label, value and hint. The provided string value must follow the BCP 47 specification (https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/bcp47).
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylanguage-ios

props.name: accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer
props.description:
A Boolean value that indicates whether or not to show the item in the large content viewer.
Available on iOS 13.0+
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilityshowslargecontentviewer

props.name: accessibilityLargeContentTitle
props.description:
When `accessibilityShowsLargeContentViewer` is set, this string will be used as title for the large content viewer.
https://reactnative.dev/docs/accessibility#accessibilitylargecontenttitle

props.name: accessibilityRespondsToUserInteraction
props.description:
Blocks the user from interacting with the component through keyboard while still allowing
screen reader to interact with it if this View is still accessible.

props.name: placement
props.description:
Where to position the tooltip - options: top, bottom, left, right, center.
Default is 'top' for tooltips rendered with children. Default is 'center' for tooltips
rendered without children. NOTE: center is only available with a childless placement,
and the content will be centered within the bounds defined by the displayInsets.

props.name: useInteractionManager
props.description:
Set this to true if you want the tooltip to wait to become visible until the callback
from InteractionManager.runAfterInteractions is executed. Can be useful if you need
to wait for navigation transitions to complete, etc

props.name: useReactNativeModal
props.description:
When false, will not use a React Native Modal component to display tooltip,
but rather an absolutely positioned view

props.name: childContentSpacing
props.description: The distance between the tooltip-rendered child and the arrow pointing to it

props.name: topAdjustment
props.description:
The top value to set for the container. This is useful to fix the issue with StatusBar in Android.
```js
  // Usage Example
  <Tooltip topAdjustment={Platform.OS === 'android' ? -StatusBar.currentHeight : 0} />
```

props.name: horizontalAdjustment
props.description:
Horizontal adjustment in pixels for the container. If for some reason the alignment of the child element we are
highlighting is off, the horizontalAdjustment prop can be used to tweak the horizontal positioning of the child
element which we are highlighting.
```js
 // Usage Example
 <Tooltip horizontalAdjustment={-84} />
```
